Read recent NWS Local Storm Reports with locations, native magnitudes/units, and remarks. These are preliminary reports, which may include estimates, corrections, or duplicate observations of the same event; they are not a complete verified event archive. Select one rolling 24/48/72-hour layer; overlapping windows are not additive. Event/state filters apply to each fetched page. No matching reports does not establish that no event occurred. Geographic bounds are followed by an exact great-circle radius filter, including dateline and polar locations. Order by distance_km for nearest reports. This compatibility form accepts options_json as a final positional argument for correlated calls on stock DuckDB 2.0.0. JSON keys match the named options on nws.main.storm_reports_near.

Read RFC precipitation normals and comparisons with PRISM normals: normal amount, observed departure from normal, or percent of normal. Default all returns three separate metrics. Negative departure indicates a deficit; 100 percent means the normal amount, not a rain probability. Read the published pixels directly, without dividing by a potentially zero normal or inferring the climatological baseline years. Periods use the source's 12Z daily accounting, not local midnight. Read NWS air-quality forecast rasters at a point, covering all published PM2.5, ozone, smoke and dust service variants. Native values and complete currently published time slices are preserved. Download and decode a native MRMS GRIB2 grid to return the nearest grid-cell value, not a rendered color. Uses native ECMWF ecCodes for regular latitude/longitude GRIB2 grids and the packing codecs enabled in that build, including PNG. Requires grib_ls and grib_get on PATH or in NWS_ECCODES_BIN. Defaults to the latest retained file and lowest available native file level; specify file_time and level to reproduce a listed file. Returns physical units and distinct missing/no-coverage/range-folded codes from NOAA's parameter table, preserving raw_value. Zero remains numeric even when a source table uses ambiguous zero codes, which are labeled. Unknown parameter codes retain raw values and NULL units. Outside the grid emits no rows. Unsupported/corrupt encodings fail explicitly. Each call reads a complete source grid: compressed downloads are bounded to 32 MiB, GRIB messages to 64 MiB, and grids to 64 million points. Native decoding is serialized per worker process with a 30-second limit per ecCodes command. Shared HTTP caching reduces repeated downloads; use GIS QPE sampling for lightweight routine rainfall queries. This compatibility form accepts options_json as a final positional argument for correlated calls on stock DuckDB 2.0.0. JSON keys match the named options on nws.main.mrms_at.

rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Compare available observed and forecast peaks without mixing units","sql":"SELECT product, max(primary_value) AS peak, primary_unit FROM nws.main.stageflow('RMDV2') GROUP BY product, primary_unit ORDER BY product"},{"description":"Compare the RMDV2 forecast crest with the gauge's flood thresholds: the highest category reached (NULL when below action stage), the next category above the crest, and the feet of headroom left","sql":"WITH crest AS (SELECT gauge_id, primary_unit, max(primary_value) AS peak_stage FROM nws.main.stageflow('RMDV2', product := 'forecast') GROUP BY gauge_id, primary_unit) SELECT c.gauge_id, c.peak_stage, c.primary_unit AS unit, max_by(t.category, t.stage) FILTER (WHERE t.stage <= c.peak_stage) AS category_reached, min_by(t.category, t.stage) FILTER (WHERE t.stage > c.peak_stage) AS next_category, min(t.stage) FILTER (WHERE t.stage > c.peak_stage) - c.peak_stage AS headroom FROM crest c JOIN nws.main.flood_thresholds('RMDV2') t ON t.gauge_id = c.gauge_id AND t.stage_unit = c.primary_unit GROUP BY c.gauge_id, c.peak_stage, c.primary_unit ORDER BY c.gauge_id"}]

Sample NOHRSC analyzed snow depth and snow water equivalent for the conterminous US. These analyses combine model estimates and assimilated observations; these are current snowpack quantities, not new snowfall or forecasts. Native GRIB snow depth is metres and snow water equivalent is kg per square metre. value_mm converts depth to millimetres or water equivalent to millimetres of liquid water (1 kg/m² = 1 mm). Read NHC/CPHC tropical development areas, forecast tracks/points/cones, watches and warnings, past tracks, wind radii/swaths, wind arrival contours, wind probability contours, peak storm surge features and coastal breakpoints. Resolve current layer IDs by exact source names. Native attributes retain product-specific units, probability ranges, wind thresholds, advisory identifiers and time wording; shared storm/advisory fields are exposed where present. A wallet is a reusable source slot, not a permanent cyclone ID. The cone describes track uncertainty, not the entire impact area; wind/probability contours overlap and must not be summed. Empty active-storm layers are legitimate. For surge inundation/tidal-mask pixels and static surge-risk scenarios, discover Mosaic Layers using map_layers and read with map_raster_at; static scenario maps are not live storm forecasts.

Download and decode a native MRMS GRIB2 grid to return the nearest grid-cell value, not a rendered color. Uses native ECMWF ecCodes for regular latitude/longitude GRIB2 grids and the packing codecs enabled in that build, including PNG. Requires grib_ls and grib_get on PATH or in NWS_ECCODES_BIN. Defaults to the latest retained file and lowest available native file level; specify file_time and level to reproduce a listed file. Returns physical units and distinct missing/no-coverage/range-folded codes from NOAA's parameter table, preserving raw_value. Zero remains numeric even when a source table uses ambiguous zero codes, which are labeled. Unknown parameter codes retain raw values and NULL units. Outside the grid emits no rows. Unsupported/corrupt encodings fail explicitly. Each call reads a complete source grid: compressed downloads are bounded to 32 MiB, GRIB messages to 64 MiB, and grids to 64 million points. Native decoding is serialized per worker process with a 30-second limit per ecCodes command. Shared HTTP caching reduces repeated downloads; use GIS QPE sampling for lightweight routine rainfall queries.

Read CPC 6–10 day, 8–14 day, monthly, or seasonal temperature/precipitation outlooks. Seasonal leads 1–13 select successive three-month windows; monthly and seasonal target_period text is retained without inventing exact timestamps. Probabilities refer to the published above/near/below-normal category, not temperature values, rainfall amounts, or the chance of any rain. Forecast dates have day precision; the last validity date is inclusive. Returns every polygon intersecting the point, including boundaries; no match means no published intersecting feature, not a guarantee of no hazard.

Read actual records from an operation discovered through api_endpoints, retaining all native JSON or original aviation text. Sample RFC gridded flash flood guidance: estimated rainfall over a selected duration that could cause small streams to flood under current soil/stream conditions. Native GRIB FFLDG values are kg/m², numerically equivalent to millimetres of water; inches are explicitly converted, never taken from a color class. Durations 1/3/6 hours have broad CONUS coverage; 12-hour guidance is regional. The discontinued 24-hour layer is rejected even if still listed. Coverage and RFC methods vary. This is guidance, not a forecast rainfall amount or an active warning. NoData remains NULL and no footprint emits no rows.

Read WPC Winter Storm Severity Index (WSSI) impact polygons for day 1, 2, 3, or days 1–3, overall or by component. Categories describe potential societal impacts, not probabilities, snow amounts, or official warnings. Overall is the maximum component impact; do not sum components. All published intersecting areas are retained. Returns every polygon intersecting the point, including boundaries; no match means no published intersecting feature, not a guarantee of no hazard. This compatibility form accepts options_json as a final positional argument for correlated calls on stock DuckDB 2.0.0. JSON keys match the named options on nws.main.winter_storm_severity_at.
